name: People thread: staff short-handed after someone quit
description: Tests thread detection + thread persistence. Prospect opens PEOPLE thread; coach must pick Play 14 follow-up and mark thread=people.
callContext:
CALL TYPE: Cold call (first contact)
EXPECTED FIRST CONTACT: Office Manager (decision maker)
COACHING DIRECTIVE: Expected to reach OM directly. If confirmed, skip gatekeeper plays — start with Play 11 (warm OM open) or jump to diagnostic.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: Hi, this is Diane, I run the front office at Harmony Dental.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Hey Diane, this is Seb with DentaVoice. Your team mentioned you handle the front desk systems. I work with practices in Salt Lake on phone coverage. Would it be unreasonable if I took two minutes?

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: How's your front desk team doing with the workload right now — enough bandwidth, or is it a stretch?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: Honestly, it's been tough. We lost Rachel two months ago and haven't been able to replace her. My girl Megan is up front by herself most days.

expectCoach.idealBehavior: Clear PEOPLE thread. Must fire Play 14 (people follow-up: 'what gives first — is it the phones?'). Must set thread=people.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: That's a lot on one person. When it gets hectic, what gives first — is it the phones?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: Yeah, phones for sure. If someone's at the counter, Megan helps them first. Phone just rings.

expectCoach.idealBehavior: Should stay in people thread. Gap question (19) is good to plant doubt, or another people follow-up. Pain math (22) is early but acceptable.
